sources.citation: Reid, Lawrence A. 2017. Re-evaluating the position of Iraya among Philippine languages. In Hsiu-chuan Liao (ed.), Issues in Austronesian Historical Linguistics (JSEALS Special Publication 1), 23-47. Honolulu: University of Hawai'i Press. hdl:10524/52405
sources.note: Nothing: no stress/accent/penult discussion (a full-text search for stress/accent full text). Iraya examples carry acute stress marks (darawá ~ darwa 'two' p.31; naҌay kadanásan ex. 26; panáy-an) but no rule is stated. Historical-comparative paper on subgrouping, pronouns, case markers.
sources.venue: Issues in Austronesian Historical Linguistics (JSEALS Special Publication 1)

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD diss., University of Hawai'i at Manoa. hdl:10125/101972
sources.note: Nothing on Iraya stress. Sec. 3.2.17 (p. 90): Iraya 'classified as a Northern Mangyan language by Zorc (1974b).. no other data is available for this language apart from the data in Zorc (1974b) and a thesis by Barbian (1977)'; Table 4.42 pronouns only.

sources.citation: Zorc, R. David. 1972. Handwritten notes on Iraya [Proto-Austronesian and Proto-Philippine worksheets, field notebooks from Baras/Binaybay, Baco and Caagutayan, San Teodoro, Or. Mindoro; typed extracts from Tweddell 1958 pp. 44-75; Tweddell's chart of ambisyllabic C-clusters]. sealang.net Zorc archive, 84 pp.
sources.note: No statement. Handwritten worksheets mark stress with an acute on nearly every Iraya word, with both penultimate and final stress attested lexically (kúyo, íya, mayáman, tíya', túwa' vs. akó, kurá, baláy, satá', tálkaka'án, ka'usún); typed Tweddell-1958 extracts (morphology, diss. pp. 44-75) show only sporadic acutes (suŋasuŋabán 'cave', butakán, agayén). Image scan, handwritten, not scanned.
